name: seek-au-job-scraper
title: Seek AU Job Scraper
pitch: Job listings from SEEK Australia (seek.com.au), straight from SEEK's own JSON search API. No browser, no proxy, so a run takes seconds.
input: Search keywords, e.g. `roof plumber` or `data engineer`. Leave empty for all jobs.
Suburb, city or region as you would type it on Seek, e.g. `Brisbane` or `All Sydney NSW`.
output: Salary text as shown on SEEK, when the ad states one
Full time, Part time, Contract/Temp, Casual/Vacation
"Join the Award Winning SE Building Solutions for…"
Up to three selling points, often empty
print_py: print(job["title"], "|", job["company"], "|", job.get("salary") or "no salary listed", "|", job["url"])
print_js: console.log(job.title, '|', job.company, '|', job.salary || 'no salary listed', '|', job.url);
uses: A fresh list of trade or office jobs in one city every morning, pushed to a Google Sheet.
Salary benchmarking by classification or region.
Lists of companies that are hiring right now (the `company` field), for sales or recruiting.
notes: Only the fields SEEK returns in search results are included; the full ad text is not.
Set `maxItems` to what you need: you pay per job returned.

name: google-trends-scraper-all-widgets
title: Google Trends Scraper
pitch: Google Trends data for up to 20 keywords per run: interest over time, interest by region and related queries, as flat rows that drop straight into Sheets, a BI tool or an AI agent. Any country or worldwide, 7 days to 5 years. No browser, no API key.
price: $0.0025 per row ($2.50 per 1,000). One keyword over 12 months produced about 170 rows in our tests.
input: Up to 20 search terms to analyse.
Two-letter country code such as `US`, `AU` or `GB`, or empty for worldwide.
output: The search term the row belongs to
Week range, region name or related query text, depending on `kind`
Unix seconds for `interest_over_time` rows; null otherwise
`related_query` rows only: whether the query is from the top or rising list
`related_query` rows only: link to that query on Google Trends
uses: Weekly demand tracking for your product category or brand in one spreadsheet.
Finding rising related queries before they peak, for content and ads.
Comparing interest across countries for market entry decisions.
notes: Rows are flat on purpose: filter on `kind` to get one table per widget.
Google Trends values are relative to the highest point in the selected period, not absolute search counts.

name: google-jobs-scraper
title: Google Jobs Scraper (US & UK)
pitch: Google Jobs results for US and UK searches: title, company, location, salary, job type, the full description and the real apply links behind each listing. Up to 10 jobs per query, with an only-new mode for scheduled runs.
input: Stop after this many jobs in total.
Skip jobs already returned by earlier runs (remembered in the `google-jobs-seen` store of your account). Ideal for schedules.
output: The job board Google sourced it from
Posting age as Google shows it
Every apply option Google lists, with its URL
Link to the listing on Google Jobs
print_py: print(job["title"], "|", job["company"], "|", job["location"], "|", job.get("salary") or "no salary listed")
print_js: console.log(job.title, '|', job.company, '|', job.location, '|', job.salary || 'no salary listed');
uses: A daily feed of new postings for a role and city with `onlyNew: true`, so you only see jobs you haven't seen.
Salary and job-type snapshots across cities.
Lists of employers hiring for a skill, with direct apply links.
notes: Google returns 10 jobs per query; use several specific queries rather than one broad one.
US and UK only. Google does not show a jobs panel for some countries, Australia included.
